claims.head: McDonagh and Cernak get the Pettersson assignment
claims.call: The Lightning’s P2 (McDonagh and Cernak) spends at least 51% of its 5-on-5 time against the Canucks’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending McDonagh and Cernak out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would. That’s Jon Cooper picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Canucks’ first line is DeBrusk, Pettersson and Lekkerimäki.
claims.nums: At home: 51% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 32% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Jon Cooper likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Canucks’ first line.

check.measure: share of Tampa Bay P2's 5-on-5 time against Vancouver L1
check.rule: held if the share is at or above the home habit; partly if above the no-matching level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Canucks give up shots, and the Lightning take them
claims.call: The Lightning take at least their usual 64.9 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
claims.body: Few teams shoot like the Lightning, and the Canucks are one of the league’s worst at keeping shots away. It could be a long night in the Canucks’ end.
claims.nums: Tampa Bay 4th for shot volume (64.9 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Vancouver 30th for shot suppression
claims.gist: The Lightning shoot a lot, and the Canucks give up plenty.

claims.head: The Canucks give up good looks, and the Lightning take them
claims.call: The Lightning’s average shot has at least their usual 6.6% chance of going in.
claims.body: The Canucks have struggled to prevent dangerous shots, and the Lightning don’t waste many.
claims.nums: Tampa Bay 8th for shot quality (a 6.6% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Vancouver 31st for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: The Lightning make their shots count, and the Canucks allow dangerous ones.

TBL.head: This one sets up well for Tampa Bay
TBL.body: Tampa Bay has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Anything short of a win would be a surprise, though Vancouver can make a game of it if they pounce on loose pucks.
